{"type":"api-request-blob","sessionId":"1e263a50-aa98-44e8-9dc0-955a7141918a","hash":"ff03d0f44ec959c5002ead7f085231f5b25ebf43ef87e28b04440da6378c4af7","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01PV9AUzuGVAq5PeyQri2KX6","type":"tool_result","content":"AGENTS.md\napp\nCLAUDE.md\nCONTEXT.md\ndata\ndev\ndocs\nnotes\npyproject.toml\nREADME.md\nscripts\nSECURITY-CHECKLIST.md\nskills\nskills-lock.json\ntemplates\ntests\ntranscripts\nuv.lock\napp/__init__.py\napp/auth.py\napp/cli.py\napp/db.py\napp/main.py\napp/markdown.py\napp/posts.py\napp/publish.py\napp/routes/__init__.py\napp/routes/admin.py\napp/routes/auth.py\napp/routes/posts.py\napp/seed.py\napp/settings.py\napp/templating.py\napp/users.py\ntests/conftest.py\ntests/test_ctx_guard.py\ntests/test_secret_key.py\ntests/test_t00.py\ntests/test_t01_login.py\ntests/test_t02_posts.py\ntests/test_usage_report.py\n# CONTEXT.md glossary\n\nProject vocabulary for the Kenyon College Finance Club (KCFC) website. One word per concept; if a better word appears, change it here.\n\n## People and roles\n\n**President**: One of the three students who run KCFC. Every President holds the Admin role.\n\n**Officer**: A club member other than a President who helps run the club. Every Officer holds the Editor role while in office.\n\n**Admin**: The role held by the three Presidents. Can create, edit, publish and delete Posts and Pages, and manage Users.\n\n**Editor**: The role held by Officers. Can create and edit Posts and save them as Drafts. Cannot publish, cannot delete a published Post, cannot touch Pages, and cannot see User management. An Editor sees and edits only their own Posts, so a sector team's writeup changes only through its own author until a President reviews it. Admins see and edit every Post.\n\n**User**: Anyone with an individual account on the admin console. Only Presidents and Officers are Users. Never shared between people.\n\n**Visitor**: Anyone reading the public site: prospective members, current members, alumni, recruiters. Visitors never log in, and everything on the public site is visible to all of them. There is no members-only content.\n\n**Sign-in**: A User signs in with their Kenyon email address and a password. A President creates the account and sets the first password face to face; there is no forced change at first sign-in. A lost password is reset by an Admin in person, never by email.\n\n**Idle sign-out**: A User is signed out automatically after about 2 hours without activity, because the Club laptop is shared at meetings.\n\n**Deactivated**: A User switched off by an Admin when their time in office ends. They can no longer sign in, and any open session ends at their next action. Their Posts keep their name as author. An Admin can reactivate them. Users are never deleted. At least one President must always stay active, and a President cannot deactivate themselves.\n\n## Content\n\n**Post**: The one kind of dated club material: a meeting announcement, a pitch writeup, or an alumni call recap. There is a single kind of Post and no categories.\n\n**Pitch writeup**: A Post presenting a stock pitch. Spring pitches are group work by sector teams, so the team members are listed in the body text. It stays a Draft until a President has reviewed it.\n\n**Sector team**: One of the three groups in the spring stock pitch competition, each covering a sector and led by one President. Teams present to Kenyon alumni working in equity research at William Blair.\n\n**Analyst Program**: The club's program for newer members. Its lasting description is an Admin-only Page.\n\n**Page**: Lasting club information: About, Leadership, Analyst Program, Join, Recruiting. Only Admins may create, edit or delete a Page; Editors cannot touch them at all.\n\n**Join Page**: The Page for prospective members: what the club does, whether prior experience is needed, how to come to a meeting.\n\n**Recruiting Page**: The Page for current members: the resume review form link and standing guides. Kept separate from the Join Page (one Page, one audience).\n\n**Homepage**: A Page edited by Admins. The next meeting (every other week, Oden 110) is the first thing a Visitor sees, followed by the contact email and the latest Posts.\n\n**Next-meeting line**: Plain text at the top of the Homepage, e.g. \"Next meeting: Wed Oct 28, 7 pm, Oden 110\". A President updates it the night before each meeting, the same habit as the email reminder. There is no calendar or automatic date logic.\n\n**Navigation**: The public menu. It lists Published Pages in an order an Admin sets, plus a link to the Posts listing.\n\n**Byline**: The public line on a Post, \"By <name>, <date>\", naming whoever posted it, never an email address. A Deactivated User's name still shows on their old Posts. Pages show no byline. Group work (such as the spring pitches by three sector teams, each led by a President) has no team field: the poster is the byline and the team members are listed in the body text.\n\n**Posts listing**: The public list of Published Posts, newest first, showing title and date.\n\n**Title convention**: A club habit, not enforced by the system: Post titles for pitches and recaps start with \"Pitch:\" or \"Recap:\" (e.g. \"Pitch: NVDA, Spring 2026\") so the Posts listing is scannable. Admins hand-link standout archive Posts from the Recruiting Page.\n\n**Event**: Not a separate thing. An event is announced in a Post.\n\n**Slug**: The short address-name of a Post or Page (e.g. `spring-stock-pitch`). Made from the title once, when first saved, and unchanged when the title is edited. Only an Admin can edit it; an old slug is not redirected.\n\n**Unpublish**: An Admin returns a Published Post or Page to Draft. It leaves the public site at the next Publish run but is kept.\n\n**Delete**: Permanent removal of a Post or Page, after an \"are you sure?\" step. Only an Admin can delete a Published Post or any Page; an Editor can delete only their own Drafts. Users are never deleted, only Deactivated (for example when seniors graduate in May: their old Posts keep their name, but they cannot log in).\n\n**Draft**: A Post that has been saved but not published. Visible only to signed-in Users, never on the public site. A Published Post returns to Draft when an Editor edits it, and stays out of the public site until an Admin publishes it again. An Admin's edit leaves it Published.\n\n**Published**: The status of a Post or Page that an Admin has approved for the public site. Approved is not the same as Live.\n\n**Publish run**: Running `cms publish`, which only an Admin does, usually right before a meeting. It rebuilds the public site from everything Published and deploys it, with no change summary. Marking an item Published has a simple \"Publish this?\" confirm on the button. A mistake is fixed by unpublishing it and running it again.\n\n**Live**: On the public site as of the last Publish run. A Published item becomes Live only at the next Publish run.\n\n**Pending changes**: Changes made since the last Publish run, which the console shows in a banner so nobody assumes saved work is already Live.\n\n**Dashboard**: The console's first screen. Shows counts of Drafts, Published items and Pending changes (Admins also see active and Deactivated Users), and a one-click \"New Post\" button.\n\n**Content list**: The console's list of Posts and Pages, newest first, filterable by status (with counts) and type. Editors see Posts only.\n\n**Preview**: The editor's side-by-side view of how the sanitized Markdown will look on the public site, labelled \"Draft, not Live\" when it is not.\n\n**Club laptop**: The one computer that runs the admin console. The console is never on the public internet; Officers sign in on it with their own accounts.\n\n## Out of scope","is_error":false}]}}

It rebuilds the public site from everything Published and deploys it, with no change summary. Marking an item Published has a simple \"Publish this?\" confirm on the button. A mistake is fixed by unpublishing it and running it again.\n\n**Live**: On the public site as of the last Publish run. A Published item becomes Live only at the next Publish run.\n\n**Pending changes**: Changes made since the last Publish run, which the console shows in a banner so nobody assumes saved work is already Live.\n\n**Dashboard**: The console's first screen. Shows counts of Drafts, Published items and Pending changes (Admins also see active and Deactivated Users), and a one-click \"New Post\" button.\n\n**Content list**: The console's list of Posts and Pages, newest first, filterable by status (with counts) and type. Editors see Posts only.\n\n**Preview**: The editor's side-by-side view of how the sanitized Markdown will look on the public site, labelled \"Draft, not Live\" when it is not.\n\n**Club laptop**: The one computer that runs the admin console. Markdown body, Draft/Published status, author, immutable slug.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nimport sqlite3\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nDRAFT = \"draft\"\nPUBLISHED = \"published\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Post:\n    id: int\n    title: str\n    slug: str\n    body: str\n    status: str\n    author_id: int\n    author_email: str\n    created_at: float\n    updated_at: float\n\n\n_SELECT = \"\"\"\nSELECT p.*, u.email AS author_email\nFROM posts p JOIN users u ON u.id = p.author_id\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef _row_to_post(row: sqlite3.Row) -> Post:\n    return Post(row[\"id\"], row[\"title\"], row[\"slug\"], row[\"body\"], row[\"status\"],\n                row[\"author_id\"], row[\"author_email\"], row[\"created_at\"], row[\"updated_at\"])\n\n\ndef slugify(title: str) -> str:\n    return re.sub(r\"[^a-z0-9]+\", \"-\", title.lower()).strip(\"-\") or \"post\"\n\n\ndef _unique_slug(conn: sqlite3.Connection, title: str) -> str:\n    base = slugify(title)\n    slug, n = base, 1\n    while conn.execute(\"SELECT 1 FROM posts WHERE slug = ?\", (slug,)).fetchone():\n        n += 1\n        slug = f\"{base}-{n}\"\n    return slug\n\n\ndef create_post(conn: sqlite3.Connection, title: str, body: str, author_id: int,\n                now: float) -> int:\n    \"\"\"New Posts are always Drafts.\"\"\"\n    with conn:\n        cur = conn.execute(\n            \"INSERT INTO posts (title, slug, body, status, author_id, created_at, updated_at)\"\n            \" VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n            (title, _unique_slug(conn, title), body, DRAFT, author_id, now, now),\n        )\n    return cur.lastrowid\n\n\ndef get_post(conn: sqlite3.Connection, post_id: int) -> Post | None:\n    row = conn.execute(_SELECT + \" WHERE p.id = ?\", (post_id,)).fetchone()\n    return _row_to_post(row) if row else None\n\n\ndef list_posts(conn: sqlite3.Connection, author_id: int | None = None) -> list[Post]:\n    \"\"\"Newest first. author_id limits the list to one User's Posts.\"\"\"\n    sql, args = _SELECT, ()\n    if author_id is not None:\n        sql, args = sql + \" WHERE p.author_id = ?\", (author_id,)\n    rows = conn.execute(sql + \" ORDER BY p.created_at DESC, p.id DESC\", args).fetchall()\n    return [_row_to_post(r) for r in rows]\n\n\ndef update_post(conn: sqlite3.Connection, post_id: int, title: str, body: str,\n                now: float, status: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"The slug is never touched here.\"\"\"\n    with conn:\n        conn.execute(\n            \"UPDATE posts SET title = ?, body = ?, status = ?, updated_at = ? WHERE id = ?\",\n            (title, body, status, now, post_id),\n        )\n\n\ndef delete_post(conn: sqlite3.Connection, post_id: int) -> None:\n    with conn:\n        conn.execute(\"DELETE FROM posts WHERE id = ?\", (post_id,))\n\"\"\"Console routes for Posts: list, create, edit, preview, delete.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Form, HTTPException, Request\nfrom fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse\n\nfrom app import auth, db, posts\nfrom app.markdown import render_markdown\nfrom app.templating import templates\n\nrouter = APIRouter(prefix=\"/admin/posts\")\n\nNOT_YOURS = \"You can only open your own Posts\"\n\n\ndef _own_post(conn, post_id: int, user) -> posts.Post:\n    \"\"\"The Post, or a refusal. Editors reach only their own; Admins reach all.\"\"\"\n    post = posts.get_post(conn, post_id)\n    if post is None:\n        # An Editor gets the same refusal as for someone else's Post, so ids do not leak.\n        if user.role != \"admin\":\n            raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail=NOT_YOURS)\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=\"No such Post\")\n    if user.role != \"admin\" and post.author_id != user.id:\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail=NOT_YOURS)\n    return post\n\n\ndef _editor_page(request, user, post, title, body, error=None, status_code=200):\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n        request, \"admin/post_edit.html\",\n        {\"title\": \"Edit Post\" if post else \"New Post\", \"user\": user, \"post\": post,\n         \"form_title\": title, \"form_body\": body, \"preview_html\": render_markdown(body),\n         \"error\": error},\n        status_code=status_code,\n    )\n\n\n@router.get(\"\")\ndef post_list(request: Request, user=Depends(auth.require_user), conn=Depends(db.get_db)):\n    own_only = None if user.role == \"admin\" else user.id\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n        request, \"admin/post_list.html\",\n        {\"title\": \"Posts\", \"user\": user, \"posts\": posts.list_posts(conn, own_only)},\n    )\n\n\n@router.get(\"/new\")\ndef post_new(request: Request, user=Depends(auth.require_user)):\n    return _editor_page(request, user, None, \"\", \"\")\n\n\n@router.post(\"\")\ndef post_create(request: Request, title: str = Form(\"\"), body: str = Form(\"\"),\n                user=Depends(auth.require_user), conn=Depends(db.get_db)):\n    title = title.strip()\n    if not title:\n        return _editor_page(request, user, None, title, body, \"A Post needs a title\", 400)\n    post_id = posts.create_post(conn, title, body, user.id, auth.now(request))\n    return RedirectResponse(f\"/admin/posts/{post_id}\", status_code=303)\n\n\n@router.post(\"/preview\")\ndef post_preview(request: Request, title: str = Form(\"\"), body: str = Form(\"\"),\n                 post_id: int | None = Form(None),\n                 user=Depends(auth.require_user), conn=Depends(db.get_db)):\n    post = _own_post(conn, post_id, user) if post_id else None\n    return _editor_page(request, user, post, title, body)\n\n\n@router.get(\"/{post_id}\")\ndef post_edit(post_id: int, request: Request, user=Depends(auth.require_user),\n              conn=Depends(db.get_db)):\n    post = _own_post(conn, post_id, user)\n    return _editor_page(request, user, post, post.title, post.body)\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{post_id}\")\ndef post_update(post_id: int, request: Request, title: str = Form(\"\"), body: str = Form(\"\"),\n                user=Depends(auth.require_user), conn=Depends(db.get_db)):\n    post = _own_post(conn, post_id, user)\n    title = title.strip()\n    if not title:\n        return _editor_page(request, user, post, title, body, \"A Post needs a title\", 400)\n    # An Editor's edit sends a Published Post back to Draft; an Admin's leaves it alone.\n    status = post.status if user.role == \"admin\" else posts.DRAFT\n    posts.update_post(conn, post_id, title, body, auth.now(request), status)\n    return RedirectResponse(f\"/admin/posts/{post_id}\", status_code=303)\n\n\ndef _deletable(post: posts.Post, user) -> posts.Post:\n    if user.role != \"admin\" and post.status != posts.DRAFT:\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail=\"Only a President can delete a Published Post\")\n    return post\n\n\n@router.get(\"/{post_id}/delete\")\ndef post_delete_confirm(post_id: int, request: Request, user=Depends(auth.require_user),\n                        conn=Depends(db.get_db)):\n    post = _deletable(_own_post(conn, post_id, user), user)\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n        request, \"admin/post_delete.html\", {\"title\": \"Delete Post\", \"user\": user, \"post\": post}\n    )\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{post_id}/delete\")\ndef post_delete(post_id: int, user=Depends(auth.require_user), conn=Depends(db.get_db)):\n    post = _deletable(_own_post(conn, post_id, user), user)\n    posts.delete_post(conn, post.id)\n    return RedirectResponse(\"/admin/posts\", status_code=303)\n\"\"\"Sessions, CSRF and the permission guard. Every admin route goes through here.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport secrets\n\nfrom fastapi import Depends, HTTPException, Request\nfrom jinja2 import pass_context\n\nfrom app import db, settings, users\n\nSAFE_METHODS = {\"GET\", \"HEAD\", \"OPTIONS\"}\n\n\nclass NotSignedIn(Exception):\n    \"\"\"Raised by the guard; the app turns it into a redirect to /login.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef ensure_csrf(request: Request) -> str:\n    token = request.session.get(\"csrf\")\n    if not token:\n        token = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)\n        request.session[\"csrf\"] = token\n    return token\n\n\n@pass_context\ndef csrf_token(context) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Use as {{ csrf_token() }} inside every state-changing form.\"\"\"\n    return ensure_csrf(context[\"request\"])\n\n\nasync def csrf_protect(request: Request) -> None:\n    \"\"\"App-wide: any request that is not GET/HEAD/OPTIONS needs a valid token.\"\"\"\n    if request.method in SAFE_METHODS:\n        return\n    if request.url.path.startswith(\"/admin\") and \"user_id\" not in request.session:\n        raise NotSignedIn  # anonymous: send to login rather than a CSRF error\n    form = await request.form()\n    sent = str(form.get(\"csrf_token\", \"\"))\n    expected = request.session.get(\"csrf\", \"\")\n    if not expected or not secrets.compare_digest(sent, expected):\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail=\"Invalid or missing CSRF token\")\n\n\ndef now(request: Request) -> float:\n    return request.app.state.clock()\n\n\ndef start_session(request: Request, user: users.User) -> None:\n    request.session.clear()  # fresh session on sign-in\n    request.session[\"user_id\"] = user.id\n    request.session[\"last_seen\"] = now(request)\n    ensure_csrf(request)\n\n\ndef end_session(request: Request) -> None:\n    request.session.clear()\n\n\ndef require_user(request: Request, conn=Depends(db.get_db)) -> users.User:\n    \"\"\"Signed in, not idle too long, and still active; otherwise to the login page.\"\"\"\n    user_id = request.session.get(\"user_id\")\n    last_seen = request.session.get(\"last_seen\")\n    current = now(request)\n    if user_id is None or last_seen is None or current - last_seen > settings.IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS:\n        end_session(request)\n        raise NotSignedIn\n    user = users.get_user(conn, user_id)\n    if user is None or not user.active:\n        end_session(request)\n        raise NotSignedIn\n    request.session[\"last_seen\"] = current\n    return user\n\n\ndef require_role(*roles: str):\n    \"\"\"Guard for role-restricted routes: Depends(require_role(\"admin\")).\"\"\"\n\n    def guard(user: users.User = Depends(require_user)) -> users.User:\n        if user.role not in roles:\n            raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail=\"You do not have access to this page\")\n        return user\n\n    return guard\ntemplates/base.html\n\ntemplates:\nadmin\nbase.html\npublic\n\ntemplates/admin:\nhello.html\nlogin.html\npost_delete.html\npost_edit.html\npost_list.html\n\ntemplates/public:\nhome.html\n\"\"\"Shared test fixtures.\n\n`client` gives you the app. `client_as(role)` gives you a client that is logged\nin as a seeded user of that role — it works as soon as your login route exists,\nso access-control tests stay one line:\n\n    def test_editor_cannot_manage_users(client_as):\n        assert client_as(\"editor\").get(\"/admin/users\").status_code in (302, 403)\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\n\nimport pytest\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n\nfrom app.main import create_app\n\n# Matches scripts/seed_demo.py. Passwords come from the environment there; in\n# tests they are fixed and meaningless.\nDEMO_USERS = {\n    \"admin\": {\"email\": \"admin@example.test\", \"password\": \"test-admin-pw\"},\n    \"editor\": {\"email\": \"editor@example.test\", \"password\": \"test-editor-pw\"},\n}\n\n\nclass FakeClock:\n    \"\"\"Injected clock so idle sign-out is tested without waiting.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, now: float = 1_000_000.0):\n        self.now = now\n\n    def __call__(self) -> float:\n        return self.now\n\n    def advance(self, seconds: float) -> None:\n        self.now += seconds\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef clock() -> FakeClock:\n    return FakeClock()\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef make_app(tmp_path, clock):\n    \"\"\"Factory for a fresh app on its own seeded database and the fake clock.\"\"\"\n    from app.seed import seed_users\n\n    def _make():\n        db = tmp_path / \"test.db\"\n        application = create_app(database=db, clock=clock)\n        seed_users(db, {role: (u[\"email\"], u[\"password\"])\n                        for role, u in DEMO_USERS.items()})\n        return application\n\n    return _make\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client(make_app) -> TestClient:\n    return TestClient(make_app())\n\n\ndef csrf_of(client: TestClient, path: str = \"/login\") -> str:\n    \"\"\"Read the CSRF token out of the form on `path`.\"\"\"\n    html = client.get(path).text\n    return re.search(r'name=\"csrf_token\" value=\"([^\"]+)\"', html).group(1)\n\n\ndef sign_in(client: TestClient, email: str, password: str, token: str | None = None):\n    return client.post(\n        \"/login\",\n        data={\"email\": email, \"password\": password,\n              \"csrf_token\": token or csrf_of(client)},\n        follow_redirects=False,\n    )\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client_as(make_app):\n    \"\"\"Return a factory: client_as(\"editor\") -> a logged-in TestClient.\"\"\"\n\n    def _login(role: str) -> TestClient:\n        user = DEMO_USERS[role]\n        c = TestClient(make_app())\n        response = sign_in(c, user[\"email\"], user[\"password\"])\n        assert response.status_code in (200, 302, 303), (\n Markdown body, Draft/Published status, author, immutable slug.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nimport sqlite3\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nDRAFT = \"draft\"\nPUBLISHED = \"published\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Post:\n    id: int\n    title: str\n    slug: str\n    body: str\n    status: str\n    author_id: int\n    author_email: str\n    created_at: float\n    updated_at: float\n\n\n_SELECT = \"\"\"\nSELECT p.*, u.email AS author_email\nFROM posts p JOIN users u ON u.id = p.author_id\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef _row_to_post(row: sqlite3.Row) -> Post:\n    return Post(row[\"id\"], row[\"title\"], row[\"slug\"], row[\"body\"], row[\"status\"],\n                row[\"author_id\"], row[\"author_email\"], row[\"created_at\"], row[\"updated_at\"])\n\n\ndef slugify(title: str) -> str:\n    return re.sub(r\"[^a-z0-9]+\", \"-\", title.lower()).strip(\"-\") or \"post\"\n\n\ndef _unique_slug(conn: sqlite3.Connection, title: str) -> str:\n    base = slugify(title)\n    slug, n = base, 1\n    while conn.execute(\"SELECT 1 FROM posts WHERE slug = ?\", (slug,)).fetchone():\n        n += 1\n        slug = f\"{base}-{n}\"\n    return slug\n\n\ndef create_post(conn: sqlite3.Connection, title: str, body: str, author_id: int,\n                now: float) -> int:\n    \"\"\"New Posts are always Drafts.\"\"\"\n    with conn:\n        cur = conn.execute(\n            \"INSERT INTO posts (title, slug, body, status, author_id, created_at, updated_at)\"\n            \" VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n            (title, _unique_slug(conn, title), body, DRAFT, author_id, now, now),\n        )\n    return cur.lastrowid\n\n\ndef get_post(conn: sqlite3.Connection, post_id: int) -> Post | None:\n    row = conn.execute(_SELECT + \" WHERE p.id = ?\", (post_id,)).fetchone()\n    return _row_to_post(row) if row else None\n\n\ndef list_posts(conn: sqlite3.Connection, author_id: int | None = None) -> list[Post]:\n    \"\"\"Newest first. author_id limits the list to one User's Posts.\"\"\"\n    sql, args = _SELECT, ()\n    if author_id is not None:\n        sql, args = sql + \" WHERE p.author_id = ?\", (author_id,)\n    rows = conn.execute(sql + \" ORDER BY p.created_at DESC, p.id DESC\", args).fetchall()\n    return [_row_to_post(r) for r in rows]\n\n\ndef update_post(conn: sqlite3.Connection, post_id: int, title: str, body: str,\n                now: float, status: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"The slug is never touched here.\"\"\"\n    with conn:\n        conn.execute(\n            \"UPDATE posts SET title = ?, body = ?, status = ?, updated_at = ? WHERE id = ?\",\n            (title, body, status, now, post_id),\n        )\n\n\ndef delete_post(conn: sqlite3.Connection, post_id: int) -> None:\n    with conn:\n        conn.execute(\"DELETE FROM posts WHERE id = ?\", (post_id,))\n\"\"\"Console routes for Posts: list, create, edit, preview, delete.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Form, HTTPException, Request\nfrom fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse\n\nfrom app import auth, db, posts\nfrom app.markdown import render_markdown\nfrom app.templating import templates\n\nrouter = APIRouter(prefix=\"/admin/posts\")\n\nNOT_YOURS = \"You can only open your own Posts\"\n\n\ndef _own_post(conn, post_id: int, user) -> posts.Post:\n    \"\"\"The Post, or a refusal. Editors reach only their own; Admins reach all.\"\"\"\n    post = posts.get_post(conn, post_id)\n    if post is None:\n        # An Editor gets the same refusal as for someone else's Post, so ids do not leak.\n        if user.role != \"admin\":\n            raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail=NOT_YOURS)\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=\"No such Post\")\n    if user.role != \"admin\" and post.author_id != user.id:\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail=NOT_YOURS)\n    return post\n\n\ndef _editor_page(request, user, post, title, body, error=None, status_code=200):\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n        request, \"admin/post_edit.html\",\n        {\"title\": \"Edit Post\" if post else \"New Post\", \"user\": user, \"post\": post,\n         \"form_title\": title, \"form_body\": body, \"preview_html\": render_markdown(body),\n         \"error\": error},\n        status_code=status_code,\n    )\n\n\n@router.get(\"\")\ndef post_list(request: Request, user=Depends(auth.require_user), conn=Depends(db.get_db)):\n    own_only = None if user.role == \"admin\" else user.id\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n        request, \"admin/post_list.html\",\n        {\"title\": \"Posts\", \"user\": user, \"posts\": posts.list_posts(conn, own_only)},\n    )\n\n\n@router.get(\"/new\")\ndef post_new(request: Request, user=Depends(auth.require_user)):\n    return _editor_page(request, user, None, \"\", \"\")\n\n\n@router.post(\"\")\ndef post_create(request: Request, title: str = Form(\"\"), body: str = Form(\"\"),\n                user=Depends(auth.require_user), conn=Depends(db.get_db)):\n    title = title.strip()\n    if not title:\n        return _editor_page(request, user, None, title, body, \"A Post needs a title\", 400)\n    post_id = posts.create_post(conn, title, body, user.id, auth.now(request))\n    return RedirectResponse(f\"/admin/posts/{post_id}\", status_code=303)\n\n\n@router.post(\"/preview\")\ndef post_preview(request: Request, title: str = Form(\"\"), body: str = Form(\"\"),\n                 post_id: int | None = Form(None),\n                 user=Depends(auth.require_user), conn=Depends(db.get_db)):\n    post = _own_post(conn, post_id, user) if post_id else None\n    return _editor_page(request, user, post, title, body)\n\n\n@router.get(\"/{post_id}\")\ndef post_edit(post_id: int, request: Request, user=Depends(auth.require_user),\n              conn=Depends(db.get_db)):\n    post = _own_post(conn, post_id, user)\n    return _editor_page(request, user, post, post.title, post.body)\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{post_id}\")\ndef post_update(post_id: int, request: Request, title: str = Form(\"\"), body: str = Form(\"\"),\n                user=Depends(auth.require_user), conn=Depends(db.get_db)):\n    post = _own_post(conn, post_id, user)\n    title = title.strip()\n    if not title:\n        return _editor_page(request, user, post, title, body, \"A Post needs a title\", 400)\n    # An Editor's edit sends a Published Post back to Draft; an Admin's leaves it alone.\n    status = post.status if user.role == \"admin\" else posts.DRAFT\n    posts.update_post(conn, post_id, title, body, auth.now(request), status)\n    return RedirectResponse(f\"/admin/posts/{post_id}\", status_code=303)\n\n\ndef _deletable(post: posts.Post, user) -> posts.Post:\n    if user.role != \"admin\" and post.status != posts.DRAFT:\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail=\"Only a President can delete a Published Post\")\n    return post\n\n\n@router.get(\"/{post_id}/delete\")\ndef post_delete_confirm(post_id: int, request: Request, user=Depends(auth.require_user),\n                        conn=Depends(db.get_db)):\n    post = _deletable(_own_post(conn, post_id, user), user)\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n        request, \"admin/post_delete.html\", {\"title\": \"Delete Post\", \"user\": user, \"post\": post}\n    )\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{post_id}/delete\")\ndef post_delete(post_id: int, user=Depends(auth.require_user), conn=Depends(db.get_db)):\n    post = _deletable(_own_post(conn, post_id, user), user)\n    posts.delete_post(conn, post.id)\n    return RedirectResponse(\"/admin/posts\", status_code=303)\n\"\"\"Sessions, CSRF and the permission guard. Every admin route goes through here.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport secrets\n\nfrom fastapi import Depends, HTTPException, Request\nfrom jinja2 import pass_context\n\nfrom app import db, settings, users\n\nSAFE_METHODS = {\"GET\", \"HEAD\", \"OPTIONS\"}\n\n\nclass NotSignedIn(Exception):\n    \"\"\"Raised by the guard; the app turns it into a redirect to /login.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef ensure_csrf(request: Request) -> str:\n    token = request.session.get(\"csrf\")\n    if not token:\n        token = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)\n        request.session[\"csrf\"] = token\n    return token\n\n\n@pass_context\ndef csrf_token(context) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Use as {{ csrf_token() }} inside every state-changing form.\"\"\"\n    return ensure_csrf(context[\"request\"])\n\n\nasync def csrf_protect(request: Request) -> None:\n    \"\"\"App-wide: any request that is not GET/HEAD/OPTIONS needs a valid token.\"\"\"\n    if request.method in SAFE_METHODS:\n        return\n    if request.url.path.startswith(\"/admin\") and \"user_id\" not in request.session:\n        raise NotSignedIn  # anonymous: send to login rather than a CSRF error\n    form = await request.form()\n    sent = str(form.get(\"csrf_token\", \"\"))\n    expected = request.session.get(\"csrf\", \"\")\n    if not expected or not secrets.compare_digest(sent, expected):\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail=\"Invalid or missing CSRF token\")\n\n\ndef now(request: Request) -> float:\n    return request.app.state.clock()\n\n\ndef start_session(request: Request, user: users.User) -> None:\n    request.session.clear()  # fresh session on sign-in\n    request.session[\"user_id\"] = user.id\n    request.session[\"last_seen\"] = now(request)\n    ensure_csrf(request)\n\n\ndef end_session(request: Request) -> None:\n    request.session.clear()\n\n\ndef require_user(request: Request, conn=Depends(db.get_db)) -> users.User:\n    \"\"\"Signed in, not idle too long, and still active; otherwise to the login page.\"\"\"\n    user_id = request.session.get(\"user_id\")\n    last_seen = request.session.get(\"last_seen\")\n    current = now(request)\n    if user_id is None or last_seen is None or current - last_seen > settings.IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS:\n        end_session(request)\n        raise NotSignedIn\n    user = users.get_user(conn, user_id)\n    if user is None or not user.active:\n        end_session(request)\n        raise NotSignedIn\n    request.session[\"last_seen\"] = current\n    return user\n\n\ndef require_role(*roles: str):\n    \"\"\"Guard for role-restricted routes: Depends(require_role(\"admin\")).\"\"\"\n\n    def guard(user: users.User = Depends(require_user)) -> users.User:\n        if user.role not in roles:\n            raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail=\"You do not have access to this page\")\n        return user\n\n    return guard\ntemplates/base.html\n\ntemplates:\nadmin\nbase.html\npublic\n\ntemplates/admin:\nhello.html\nlogin.html\npost_delete.html\npost_edit.html\npost_list.html\n\ntemplates/public:\nhome.html\n\"\"\"Shared test fixtures.\n\n`client` gives you the app. `client_as(role)` gives you a client that is logged\nin as a seeded user of that role — it works as soon as your login route exists,\nso access-control tests stay one line:\n\n    def test_editor_cannot_manage_users(client_as):\n        assert client_as(\"editor\").get(\"/admin/users\").status_code in (302, 403)\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\n\nimport pytest\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n\nfrom app.main import create_app\n\n# Matches scripts/seed_demo.py. Passwords come from the environment there; in\n# tests they are fixed and meaningless.\nDEMO_USERS = {\n    \"admin\": {\"email\": \"admin@example.test\", \"password\": \"test-admin-pw\"},\n    \"editor\": {\"email\": \"editor@example.test\", \"password\": \"test-editor-pw\"},\n}\n\n\nclass FakeClock:\n    \"\"\"Injected clock so idle sign-out is tested without waiting.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, now: float = 1_000_000.0):\n        self.now = now\n\n    def __call__(self) -> float:\n        return self.now\n\n    def advance(self, seconds: float) -> None:\n        self.now += seconds\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef clock() -> FakeClock:\n    return FakeClock()\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef make_app(tmp_path, clock):\n    \"\"\"Factory for a fresh app on its own seeded database and the fake clock.\"\"\"\n    from app.seed import seed_users\n\n    def _make():\n        db = tmp_path / \"test.db\"\n        application = create_app(database=db, clock=clock)\n        seed_users(db, {role: (u[\"email\"], u[\"password\"])\n                        for role, u in DEMO_USERS.items()})\n        return application\n\n    return _make\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client(make_app) -> TestClient:\n    return TestClient(make_app())\n\n\ndef csrf_of(client: TestClient, path: str = \"/login\") -> str:\n    \"\"\"Read the CSRF token out of the form on `path`.\"\"\"\n    html = client.get(path).text\n    return re.search(r'name=\"csrf_token\" value=\"([^\"]+)\"', html).group(1)\n\n\ndef sign_in(client: TestClient, email: str, password: str, token: str | None = None):\n    return client.post(\n        \"/login\",\n        data={\"email\": email, \"password\": password,\n              \"csrf_token\": token or csrf_of(client)},\n        follow_redirects=False,\n    )\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client_as(make_app):\n    \"\"\"Return a factory: client_as(\"editor\") -> a logged-in TestClient.\"\"\"\n\n    def _login(role: str) -> TestClient:\n        user = DEMO_USERS[role]\n        c = TestClient(make_app())\n        response = sign_in(c, user[\"email\"], user[\"password\"])\n        assert response.status_code in (200, 302, 303), (\n            f\"Login as {role} failed with {response.status_code}\")\n        return c\n\n    return _login\n\"\"\"T02: Officers write and edit their own Post drafts. {"type":"api-request-blob","sessionId":"1e263a50-aa98-44e8-9dc0-955a7141918a","hash":"9d5f4c473400945f2a8dddd67ec45681d06db8903fbba38e5ec21090833ceec6","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01TM1oJ6qksXcRXDbEpwDoxa","type":"tool_result","content":"{% extends \"base.html\" %}\n{% block content %}\n  <h1>{{ title }}</h1>\n  <p><a href=\"/admin/posts\">All Posts</a></p>\n  {% if error %}<p role=\"alert\">{{ error }}</p>{% endif %}\n  <div style=\"display: flex; gap: 1rem; flex-wrap: wrap;\">\n    <form method=\"post\" action=\"{{ '/admin/posts/' ~ post.id if post else '/admin/posts' }}\"\n          style=\"flex: 1 1 20rem;\">\n      <input type=\"hidden\" name=\"csrf_token\" value=\"{{ csrf_token() }}\">\n      {% if post %}<input type=\"hidden\" name=\"post_id\" value=\"{{ post.id }}\">{% endif %}\n      <p><label>Title<br>\n        <input type=\"text\" name=\"title\" value=\"{{ form_title }}\" required style=\"width: 100%;\"></label></p>\n      {% if post %}\n      <p>Slug: <code>{{ post.slug }}</code> (set when first saved)</p>\n      <p>Status: {{ post.status | capitalize }}</p>\n      {% endif %}\n      <p><label>Body (Markdown)<br>\n        <textarea name=\"body\" rows=\"14\" style=\"width: 100%;\">{{ form_body }}</textarea></label></p>\n      <p>\n        <button type=\"submit\">Save Draft</button>\n        <button type=\"submit\" formaction=\"/admin/posts/preview\">Preview</button>\n      </p>\n    </form>\n    <section style=\"flex: 1 1 20rem;\" aria-label=\"Preview\">\n      <h2>Preview</h2>\n      {% if not post or post.status == 'draft' %}\n      <p><strong>Draft, not Live</strong></p>\n      {% else %}\n      <p><strong>Published</strong> (Live after the next Publish run)</p>\n      {% endif %}\n      {{ preview_html | safe }}\n    </section>\n  </div>\n  {% if post %}<p><a href=\"/admin/posts/{{ post.id }}/delete\">Delete this Post</a></p>{% endif %}\n{% endblock %}\n{% extends \"base.html\" %}\n{% block content %}\n  <h1>Delete this Post?</h1>\n  <p>Are you sure you want to permanently delete “{{ post.title }}”? This cannot be undone.</p>\n  <form method=\"post\" action=\"/admin/posts/{{ post.id }}/delete\">\n    <input type=\"hidden\" name=\"csrf_token\" value=\"{{ csrf_token() }}\">\n    <button type=\"submit\">Yes, delete it</button>\n    <a href=\"/admin/posts/{{ post.id }}\">Cancel</a>\n  </form>\n{% endblock %}\n{% extends \"base.html\" %}\n{% block content %}\n  <h1>Posts</h1>\n  <p><a href=\"/admin/posts/new\">New Post</a> · <a href=\"/admin\">Dashboard</a></p>\n  {% if posts %}\n  <ul>\n    {% for post in posts %}\n    <li>\n      <a href=\"/admin/posts/{{ post.id }}\">{{ post.title }}</a>\n      — {{ post.status | capitalize }}, by {{ post.author_email }}\n    </li>\n    {% endfor %}\n  </ul>\n  {% else %}\n  <p>No Posts yet.</p>\n  {% endif %}\n{% endblock %}\ndef test_president_opens_and_edits_any_post(client_as, make_app):\n    editor = client_as(\"editor\")\n    url = post_url(create_post(editor, title=\"Pitch: NVDA\"))\n    # Same app and database, signed in as the President.\n    from fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n    from tests.conftest import sign_in\n    admin = TestClient(editor.app)\n    sign_in(admin, \"admin@example.test\", \"test-admin-pw\")\n    assert \"Pitch: NVDA\" in admin.get(\"/admin/posts\").text\n    token = csrf_of(admin, url)\n    admin.post(url, data={\"title\": \"Pitch: NVDA (reviewed)\", \"body\": \"ok\", \"csrf_token\": token})\n    assert \"Pitch: NVDA (reviewed)\" in admin.get(url).text\n\n\ndef test_officer_deletes_own_draft_after_an_are_you_sure_step(client_as):\n    c = client_as(\"editor\")\n    url = post_url(create_post(c, title=\"Abandoned idea\"))\n    confirm = c.get(url + \"/delete\")\n    assert confirm.status_code == 200\n    assert \"Are you sure\" in confirm.text\n    assert \"Abandoned idea\" in c.get(\"/admin/posts\").text  # a GET deletes nothing\n    token = csrf_of(c, url + \"/delete\")\n    done = c.post(url + \"/delete\", data={\"csrf_token\": token}, follow_redirects=False)\n    assert done.status_code == 303\n    assert \"Abandoned idea\" not in c.get(\"/admin/posts\").text\n    assert c.get(url).status_code == 403  # gone, and an Officer cannot tell gone from not theirs\n\n\ndef test_every_post_form_carries_a_csrf_token_and_rejects_without_it(client_as):\n    c = client_as(\"editor\")\n    url = post_url(create_post(c))\n    for path in (\"/admin/posts/new\", url, url + \"/delete\"):\n        assert 'name=\"csrf_token\"' in c.get(path).text, path\n    for path in (\"/admin/posts\", url, url + \"/delete\", \"/admin/posts/preview\"):\n        response = c.post(path, data={\"title\": \"x\", \"body\": \"y\"})\n        assert response.status_code == 403, path\n    assert c.get(url).status_code == 200\n\n\ndef test_posts_are_reachable_from_the_console_home(client_as):\n    assert \"/admin/posts\" in client_as(\"editor\").get(\"/admin\").text\n25:def create_app(database: Path | None = None,\n28:    database = Path(database or settings.DATABASE_PATH)\n32:        db.init_db(database)\n37:    app.state.database = database","is_error":false}]}}

president_for(editor) -> TestClient:\n    \"\"\"A President on the same app and database as `editor`.\"\"\"\n    admin = TestClient(editor.app)\n    sign_in(admin, \"admin@example.test\", \"test-admin-pw\")\n    return admin\n\n\ndef act(c, url, action, **extra):\n    token = csrf_of(c, url)\n    return c.post(f\"{url}/{action}\", data={\"csrf_token\": token, **extra},\n                  follow_redirects=False)\n\n\ndef published_post(editor, title=\"Pitch: NVDA\"):\n    url = post_url(create_post(editor, title=title))\n    admin = president_for(editor)\n    assert act(admin, url, client_as(\"editor\")\n    url = post_url(create_post(editor))\n    admin = president_for(editor)\n    confirm = admin.get(url + \"/publish\")\n    assert confirm.status_code == 200\n    assert \"Publish this?\" in confirm.text\n    assert 'name=\"csrf_token\"' in confirm.text\n    assert \"Status: Draft\" in admin.get(url).text  # a GET publishes nothing\n    assert act(admin, url, \"publish\").status_code == 303\n    assert \"Status: Published\" in admin.get(url).text\n\n\ndef test_officer_cannot_publish_even_by_direct_post(client_as):\n    editor = client_as(\"editor\")\n    url = post_url(create_post(editor))\n    assert editor.get(url + \"/publish\").status_code == 403\n    assert act(editor, url, \"publish\").status_code == 403\n    assert \"Status: Draft\" in editor.get(url).text\n\n\ndef test_president_unpublishes_a_published_post(client_as):\n    editor = client_as(\"editor\")\n    url, admin = published_post(editor)\n    confirm = admin.get(url + \"/unpublish\")\n    assert \"Are you sure\" in confirm.text\n    assert act(admin, url, \"unpublish\").status_code == 303\n    assert \"Status: Draft\" in admin.get(url).text\n\n\ndef test_officer_cannot_unpublish(client_as):\n    editor = client_as(\"editor\")\n    url, admin = published_post(editor)\n    assert act(editor, url, \"unpublish\").status_code == 403\n    assert \"Status: Published\" in admin.get(url).text\n\n\ndef test_officers_edit_turns_a_published_post_back_to_draft(client_as):\n    editor = client_as(\"editor\")\n    url, admin = published_post(editor)\n    token = csrf_of(editor, url)\n    editor.post(url, data={\"title\": \"Pitch: NVDA\", \"body\": \"changed\", \"csrf_token\": token})\n    assert \"Status: Draft\" in admin.get(url).text\n\n\ndef test_presidents_edit_keeps_a_published_post_published(client_as):\n    editor = client_as(\"editor\")\n    url, admin = published_post(editor)\n    token = csrf_of(admin, url)\n    admin.post(url, data={\"title\": \"Pitch: NVDA\", \"body\": \"reviewed\", \"csrf_token\": token})\n    assert \"Status: Published\" in admin.get(url).text\n\n\ndef test_only_a_president_can_delete_a_published_post(client_as):\n    editor = client_as(\"editor\")\n    url, admin = published_post(editor)\n    assert editor.get(url + \"/delete\").status_code == 403\n    assert act(editor, url, \"delete\").status_code == 403\n    assert \"Pitch: NVDA\" in admin.get(\"/admin/posts\").text\n    assert \"Are you sure\" in admin.get(url + \"/delete\").text\n    assert act(admin, url, \"delete\").status_code == 303\n    assert \"Pitch: NVDA\" not in admin.get(\"/admin/posts\").text\n    assert admin.get(url).status_code == 404\n\n\ndef test_president_deletes_any_draft_after_a_confirm(client_as):\n    editor = client_as(\"editor\")\n    url = post_url(create_post(editor, title=\"Their draft\"))\n    admin = president_for(editor)\n    assert \"Are you sure\" in admin.get(url + \"/delete\").text\n    assert act(admin, url, \"delete\").status_code == 303\n    assert \"Their draft\" not in admin.get(\"/admin/posts\").text\n\n\ndef test_only_a_president_can_edit_a_slug(client_as):\n    editor = client_as(\"editor\")\n    url = post_url(create_post(editor, title=\"Alumni call\"))\n    admin = president_for(editor)\n    page = admin.get(url).text\n    assert 'name=\"slug\"' in page\n    token = csrf_of(admin, url)\n    admin.post(url, data={\"title\": \"Alumni call\", \"body\": \"x\", \"slug\": \"William Blair Recap\",\n data={\"title\": \"Alumni call\", \"body\": \"x\", \"slug\": \"hacked\",\n                           \"csrf_token\": token})\n    page = editor.get(url).text\n    assert \"william-blair-recap\" in page\n    assert \"hacked\" not in page\n\n\ndef test_slug_cannot_collide_with_another_post(client_as):\n    editor = client_as(\"editor\")\n    post_url(create_post(editor, title=\"Taken\"))\n    url If not, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in the tracker doc.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nSearch the repo for every file that documents how code should be written. When `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md` exists, it must be on the list.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\nIssue both sub-agent calls together, in the foreground, and aggregate the reports they return.\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n"}]}}

The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>\n<result>**Review of the uncommitted T03 diff (read-only, nothing edited)**\n\n**(a) Violations of documented standards**\n\nNo hard violations of CLAUDE.md's hard constraints.\n- The new `post_confirm.html` form carries `csrf_token`.\n- Its `action=\"/admin/posts/...\"` is console HTML, so the relative-path rule for published HTML doesn't apply.\n- Access control is enforced in code through `auth.require_role(\"admin\")` (SECURITY-CHECKLIST #4 and #10).\n- I couldn't find a secrets problem.\n\nJudgement-level standards items:\n- **`templates/admin/post_edit.html`, slug block.** For admins the hunk renders an editable `Slug` input and then a redundant `Slug: &lt;code&gt;…&lt;/code&gt;` line. That is a UI bug. The test asserts `Slug: &lt;code&gt;other&lt;/code&gt;` and so depends on the duplicate.\n- **`CONTEXT.md` vocabulary.** The hunk `\"Publish this?\"` matches the glossary. `\"Are you sure you want to unpublish this?\"` is fine. The `CONFIRMS` comment says \"Live\", which is used correctly. The tests and a docstring use \"president_for\", which is fine. The word \"Slug\" in the confirm flow is consistent.\n- **`app/routes/posts.py`, non-atomic slug update.** `post_update` calls `update_post` and then `set_slug` in separate transactions. If `set_slug` fails, for example a UNIQUE race after the `slug_taken` check, the post is saved but the slug is not. This is a correctness risk rather than a rule breach. I did not check whether `posts.slug` has a UNIQUE constraint.\n- **`app/routes/posts.py`, silent slug skip.** An admin who submits a blank slug gets it silently ignored. An editor's slug field is also silently ignored. The second is consistent with the test.\n\n**(b) Baseline smells (all judgement calls)**\n\n- **Primitive Obsession / Data Clumps, `CONFIRMS`.** It is a positional 5-tuple, `(\"Publish this?\", \"Yes, publish it\", posts.DRAFT, posts.PUBLISHED, \"It becomes Live…\")`. It is unpacked as `heading, button, _, _, note` and `_, _, from_status, to_status, _`, so callers depend on field order. A small dataclass or NamedTuple would fix this. Action names are also bare strings that are repeated in the URLs and the template.\n- **Repeated Switches / Shotgun Surgery.** The `user.role == 'admin'` check appears in the routes (`post_update`, `_own_post`, `_deletable`, `post_list`) and in the templates (`post_edit.html`, three times). Adding a role means changing all of them. A `can_publish` or `can_edit_slug` flag passed to the template would help.\n- **Duplicated Code.** The two confirm GET handlers and the two POST handlers are identical wrappers. Only the action string differs. A parametrised route such as `/{post_id}/{action:publish|unpublish}` would halve them. `post_delete_confirm` also duplicates `_confirm_page` in structure.\n- **Duplicated Code, SQL.** `slug_taken` repeats the `SELECT 1 FROM posts WHERE slug = ?` pattern from `_unique_slug`. The `set_status` and `update_post` UPDATE statements overlap.\n- **Mysterious Name.** `admin_only` is a module-level `Depends(...)` object. It is easy to mistake for a function. `CONFIRMS` doesn't say what it holds. `_change_status` quietly does nothing when the from-status doesn't match (an idempotent no-op), and the name doesn't convey that.\n- **Feature Envy.** `_change_status` and `_confirm_page` mainly manipulate `CONFIRMS` data. That suggests a model object for the transition.\n- **Divergent Change.** `app/routes/posts.py` now handles editing, slugs, status transitions and deletion in one module. This is mild at the current size.\n- **Tests, Duplicated Code.** `act(...)` and the repeated `csrf_of` plus `post` pattern recur in several tests. The `post_edit` calls could use a helper.\n\nNo Speculative Generality, Middle Man, Message Chains or Refused Bequest spotted. Nothing here calls for code-review blocking beyond the duplicate slug line and the non-atomic slug write.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>46382</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>2</tool_uses><duration_ms>17899</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"}

The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>\n<result>**Review of the uncommitted T03 diff (read-only, nothing edited)**\n\n**(a) Violations of documented standards**\n\nNo hard violations of CLAUDE.md's hard constraints.\n- The new `post_confirm.html` form carries `csrf_token`.\n- Its `action=\"/admin/posts/...\"` is console HTML, so the relative-path rule for published HTML doesn't apply.\n- Access control is enforced in code through `auth.require_role(\"admin\")` (SECURITY-CHECKLIST #4 and #10).\n- I couldn't find a secrets problem.\n\nJudgement-level standards items:\n- **`templates/admin/post_edit.html`, slug block.** For admins the hunk renders an editable `Slug` input and then a redundant `Slug: &lt;code&gt;…&lt;/code&gt;` line. That is a UI bug. The test asserts `Slug: &lt;code&gt;other&lt;/code&gt;` and so depends on the duplicate.\n- **`CONTEXT.md` vocabulary.** The hunk `\"Publish this?\"` matches the glossary. `\"Are you sure you want to unpublish this?\"` is fine. The `CONFIRMS` comment says \"Live\", which is used correctly. The tests and a docstring use \"president_for\", which is fine. The word \"Slug\" in the confirm flow is consistent.\n- **`app/routes/posts.py`, non-atomic slug update.** `post_update` calls `update_post` and then `set_slug` in separate transactions. If `set_slug` fails, for example a UNIQUE race after the `slug_taken` check, the post is saved but the slug is not. This is a correctness risk rather than a rule breach. I did not check whether `posts.slug` has a UNIQUE constraint.\n- **`app/routes/posts.py`, silent slug skip.** An admin who submits a blank slug gets it silently ignored. An editor's slug field is also silently ignored. The second is consistent with the test.\n\n**(b) Baseline smells (all judgement calls)**\n\n- **Primitive Obsession / Data Clumps, `CONFIRMS`.** It is a positional 5-tuple, `(\"Publish this?\", \"Yes, publish it\", posts.DRAFT, posts.PUBLISHED, \"It becomes Live…\")`. It is unpacked as `heading, button, _, _, note` and `_, _, from_status, to_status, _`, so callers depend on field order. A small dataclass or NamedTuple would fix this. Action names are also bare strings that are repeated in the URLs and the template.\n- **Repeated Switches / Shotgun Surgery.** The `user.role == 'admin'` check appears in the routes (`post_update`, `_own_post`, `_deletable`, `post_list`) and in the templates (`post_edit.html`, three times). Adding a role means changing all of them. A `can_publish` or `can_edit_slug` flag passed to the template would help.\n- **Duplicated Code.** The two confirm GET handlers and the two POST handlers are identical wrappers. Only the action string differs. A parametrised route such as `/{post_id}/{action:publish|unpublish}` would halve them. `post_delete_confirm` also duplicates `_confirm_page` in structure.\n- **Duplicated Code, SQL.** `slug_taken` repeats the `SELECT 1 FROM posts WHERE slug = ?` pattern from `_unique_slug`. The `set_status` and `update_post` UPDATE statements overlap.\n- **Mysterious Name.** `admin_only` is a module-level `Depends(...)` object. It is easy to mistake for a function. `CONFIRMS` doesn't say what it holds. `_change_status` quietly does nothing when the from-status doesn't match (an idempotent no-op), and the name doesn't convey that.\n- **Feature Envy.** `_change_status` and `_confirm_page` mainly manipulate `CONFIRMS` data. That suggests a model object for the transition.\n- **Divergent Change.** `app/routes/posts.py` now handles editing, slugs, status transitions and deletion in one module. This is mild at the current size.\n- **Tests, Duplicated Code.** `act(...)` and the repeated `csrf_of` plus `post` pattern recur in several tests. The `post_edit` calls could use a helper.\n\nNo Speculative Generality, Middle Man, Message Chains or Refused Bequest spotted. Nothing here calls for code-review blocking beyond the duplicate slug line and the non-atomic slug write.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>46382</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>2</tool_uses><duration_ms>17899</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"},"uuid":"9e96e5f2-119c-4648-8882-fcf98bb15be2","timestamp":"2026-10-15T03:46:11.249Z","permissionMode":"bypassPermissions","origin":{"kind":"task-notification","producer":"session-task","runId":"0mv8zxr6a-4147b9b8"},"promptSource":"system","turnOrigin":"task_notification","turnPosition":{"promptIndex":1,"turnIndex":2},"queueSkipAttachments":true,"userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/biswas1/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"1e263a50-aa98-44e8-9dc0-955a7141918a","version":"2.1.300","gitBranch":"main"}

The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>\n<result>**Review of the uncommitted T03 change against #4 and #1** (read-only; I did not run the tests because `python` isn't on the PATH here)\n\n**(a) Missing or partial**\n- **Delete confirm and CSRF.** The ticket says \"All confirms are CSRF-protected\". The only evidence is `test_confirm_posts_reject_missing_csrf`, and it assumes CSRF is enforced by middleware. I couldn't confirm that from the diff.\n- **Slug test coverage.** Spec #1 says \"Tests cover every Admin/Editor combination\". Two combinations are missing:\n  - No test checks that an Editor's slug attempt on a Published Post is ignored.\n  - The admin slug test never sends an empty or whitespace slug.\n- **Slug normalisation is untested.** Spec #1 says \"unique, immutable on title edit\". `slugify(\"!!!\")` returns `\"post\"`, so an Admin typing punctuation silently gets `post`. If that collides, the user sees an \"already used\" message for a slug they never typed.\n- **Slug template.** The Admin edit page shows the slug twice, once in the input and once as \"Slug: &lt;code&gt;\" text. The second looks like a leftover that only exists to satisfy a test assertion.\n- **Carried-over test 1 (Officer edit turns Published back to Draft).** `test_officers_edit_turns_a_published_post_back_to_draft` is present, but it never checks the response status. If the POST failed, the Post would still be Published and the test would fail, so it works. It would still read better with a 303 assert.\n- **Carried-over test 2 (only a President deletes a Published Post).** `test_only_a_president_can_delete_a_published_post` is present and correct.\n\n**(b) Scope creep**\n- **Server-side state guard.** `_change_status` quietly does nothing when the Post is already in the target state, then redirects. Spec #1 doesn't ask for this. It isn't harmful, but it is untested and gives no feedback.\n- **Slug uniqueness check.** `slug_taken` and the 400 error page go beyond #4. They are justified by #1's \"unique\", so keep them, but they are unrequested for this ticket.\n- **Unpublish wording.** The unpublish text \"leaves the public site at the next Publish run\" is invented behaviour copy. It matches #1's \"fixed by unpublishing and running it again\", so it is low risk.\n\n**(c) Looks implemented but may be wrong**\n- **Editor probing ids.** `_own_post` returns 403 for a missing id when the user is an Editor, and 404 for an Admin. The confirm routes use `admin_only`, so an Editor gets a generic 403 there. That is consistent with \"Editor-restricted requests return a refusal\".\n- **Non-existent Post.** An Admin gets a 404 on a missing id, and `test_only_a_president_can_delete_a_published_post` relies on it. That is fine.\n- **Slug race and partial update.** `update_post` and `set_slug` run in two separate transactions. If the slug update fails (for example, a UNIQUE violation from a race), the title and body are already saved and the user sees a 500. This should be one transaction. The `slug_taken` check also isn't atomic with the write.\n- **Slug accepted from non-Admins.** The `slug` form field is parsed for everyone but only used when `user.role == \"admin\"`. That is safe.\n- **Slug changed on a Published Post.** Spec #1 says \"no redirects from old slugs\", so an Admin renaming the slug of a Live Post breaks existing links. That is acceptable per spec, but there's no warning in the UI.\n- **Unused status tuple fields.** `CONFIRMS` carries `from_status` and `to_status`. Unpublishing a Draft is silently ignored, but the Unpublish link only renders for Published Posts, so that is only reachable by direct URL. Harmless.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>49162</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>4</tool_uses><duration_ms>19525</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"}

The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>\n<result>**Review of the uncommitted T03 change against #4 and #1** (read-only; I did not run the tests because `python` isn't on the PATH here)\n\n**(a) Missing or partial**\n- **Delete confirm and CSRF.** The ticket says \"All confirms are CSRF-protected\". The only evidence is `test_confirm_posts_reject_missing_csrf`, and it assumes CSRF is enforced by middleware. I couldn't confirm that from the diff.\n- **Slug test coverage.** Spec #1 says \"Tests cover every Admin/Editor combination\". Two combinations are missing:\n  - No test checks that an Editor's slug attempt on a Published Post is ignored.\n  - The admin slug test never sends an empty or whitespace slug.\n- **Slug normalisation is untested.** Spec #1 says \"unique, immutable on title edit\". `slugify(\"!!!\")` returns `\"post\"`, so an Admin typing punctuation silently gets `post`. If that collides, the user sees an \"already used\" message for a slug they never typed.\n- **Slug template.** The Admin edit page shows the slug twice, once in the input and once as \"Slug: &lt;code&gt;\" text. The second looks like a leftover that only exists to satisfy a test assertion.\n- **Carried-over test 1 (Officer edit turns Published back to Draft).** `test_officers_edit_turns_a_published_post_back_to_draft` is present, but it never checks the response status. If the POST failed, the Post would still be Published and the test would fail, so it works. It would still read better with a 303 assert.\n- **Carried-over test 2 (only a President deletes a Published Post).** `test_only_a_president_can_delete_a_published_post` is present and correct.\n\n**(b) Scope creep**\n- **Server-side state guard.** `_change_status` quietly does nothing when the Post is already in the target state, then redirects. Spec #1 doesn't ask for this. It isn't harmful, but it is untested and gives no feedback.\n- **Slug uniqueness check.** `slug_taken` and the 400 error page go beyond #4. They are justified by #1's \"unique\", so keep them, but they are unrequested for this ticket.\n- **Unpublish wording.** The unpublish text \"leaves the public site at the next Publish run\" is invented behaviour copy. It matches #1's \"fixed by unpublishing and running it again\", so it is low risk.\n\n**(c) Looks implemented but may be wrong**\n- **Editor probing ids.** `_own_post` returns 403 for a missing id when the user is an Editor, and 404 for an Admin. The confirm routes use `admin_only`, so an Editor gets a generic 403 there. That is consistent with \"Editor-restricted requests return a refusal\".\n- **Non-existent Post.** An Admin gets a 404 on a missing id, and `test_only_a_president_can_delete_a_published_post` relies on it. That is fine.\n- **Slug race and partial update.** `update_post` and `set_slug` run in two separate transactions. If the slug update fails (for example, a UNIQUE violation from a race), the title and body are already saved and the user sees a 500. This should be one transaction. The `slug_taken` check also isn't atomic with the write.\n- **Slug accepted from non-Admins.** The `slug` form field is parsed for everyone but only used when `user.role == \"admin\"`. That is safe.\n- **Slug changed on a Published Post.** Spec #1 says \"no redirects from old slugs\", so an Admin renaming the slug of a Live Post breaks existing links. That is acceptable per spec, but there's no warning in the UI.\n- **Unused status tuple fields.** `CONFIRMS` carries `from_status` and `to_status`. Unpublishing a Draft is silently ignored, but the Unpublish link only renders for Published Posts, so that is only reachable by direct URL. Harmless.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>49162</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>4</tool_uses><duration_ms>19525</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"},"uuid":"b54e43cd-bef1-4a6b-b0c6-e662c9ea34a8","timestamp":"2026-10-15T03:46:14.649Z","permissionMode":"bypassPermissions","origin":{"kind":"task-notification","producer":"session-task","runId":"0mv8zxsiq-3aa0f3aa"},"promptSource":"system","turnOrigin":"task_notification","turnPosition":{"promptIndex":1,"turnIndex":3},"queueSkipAttachments":true,"userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/biswas1/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"1e263a50-aa98-44e8-9dc0-955a7141918a","version":"2.1.300","gitBranch":"main"}

revisit if a third action or role appears.\n\n**Spec**\n- Missing coverage: an Officer's slug attempt on a Published Post, and a blank slug from a President. **Fixed**: two tests added.\n- The carried-over Officer-edit test did not assert the response status. **Fixed**: it now asserts 303.\n- Publish/Unpublish on a Post already in the target state is a silent no-op. **Skipped**: harmless and only reachable by direct URL.\n- A slug rename on a Live Post breaks old links. **Skipped**: matches the spec (\"an old slug is not redirected\").\n- CSRF on the new confirms: covered by `test_confirm_posts_reject_missing_csrf`, which posts without a token to publish, unpublish and delete, and the app-wide `csrf_protect` dependency.\n\nTests: 67 passed (13 new in `tests/test_t03_president_control.py`, including the two carried over from T02).\nEOF\nrm -f /tmp/x\ngh issue comment 4 --body-file \"/private/tmp/claude-503/-Users-biswas1-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/1e263a50-aa98-44e8-9dc0-955a7141918a/scratchpad/comment.md\" && git add app templates tests && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'\nT03: Presidents publish, unpublish and delete Posts\n\nPublish, Unpublish and Delete behind confirms (Admin only for publish and\nunpublish), Admin-only slug editing, and tests for the Officer-edit-to-Draft\nand President-only-delete-of-Published rules carried over from T02.\n\nCloses #4\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\ngit push 2>&1 | tail -3; the test now checks the input value.\n- `update_post` then `set_slug` ran as two transactions, so a failed slug write could leave title/body saved. **Fixed**: `update_post` takes an optional slug and writes everything in one transaction; `set_slug` removed.\n- `CONFIRMS` is a positional 5-tuple, the publish/unpublish handlers are duplicated, and `user.role == 'admin'` is repeated in routes and templates (judgement-call smells). **Skipped**: small and readable at this size; revisit if a third action or role appears.\n\n**Spec**\n- Missing coverage: an Officer's slug attempt on a Published Post, and a blank slug from a President. **Fixed**: two tests added.\n- The carried-over Officer-edit test did not assert the response status. **Fixed**: it now asserts 303.\n- Publish/Unpublish on a Post already in the target state is a silent no-op. **Skipped**: harmless and only reachable by direct URL.\n- A slug rename on a Live Post breaks old links. **Skipped**: matches the spec (\"an old slug is not redirected\").\n- CSRF on the new confirms: covered by `test_confirm_posts_reject_missing_csrf` (publish, unpublish, delete without a token are refused) plus the app-wide `csrf_protect` dependency.\n\nTests: 67 passed (13 new in `tests/test_t03_president_control.py`, including the two carried over from T02).\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"4e150e6e-02f3-4d13-b8aa-4f091af233ff","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"mode"},"session_id":"1e263a50-aa98-44e8-9dc0-955a7141918a","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/biswas1/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"1e263a50-aa98-44e8-9dc0-955a7141918a","version":"2.1.300","gitBranch":"main"}

I couldn't run `ruff` because it isn't installed in the project environment.\n\nWhat now works:\n- **Publish and Unpublish:** a President publishes a Draft after a \"Publish this?\" confirm and unpublishes after an \"Are you sure\" confirm. An Officer's direct POST or GET to either is refused with a 403.\n- **Delete:** a President can delete any Post after the confirm. An Officer can delete only their own Drafts.\n- **Edits:** an Officer's edit turns a Published Post back to Draft, while a President's edit keeps it Published.\n- **Slugs:** only a President sees and can change the slug. An Officer's attempt is ignored, and a slug already used by another Post is refused with a 400.\n- **CSRF:** all the new confirms reject a request without a token.\n- **Carried-over T02 tests:** both are in, covering the Officer edit back to Draft and the President-only delete of a Published Post.\n\nI posted the `/code-review` findings and how each was resolved as a comment on #4, before committing.\n- **Fixed:**\n  - The slug showed twice on a President's edit page.\n  - The title/body save and the slug save are now one transaction.\n  - Two missing slug tests were added.\n  - The Officer-edit test now checks for a 303.\n- **Skipped:**\n  - The positional `CONFIRMS` tuple and the repeated `role == 'admin'` checks.\n  - The silent no-op when a Post is already in the target state.\n  - The broken old link after a slug rename, which the spec accepts.\n\n- **Ledger file:** `notes/usage-ledger.csv` is modified (the ledger hook changes it) and I left it out of the T03 commit, as earlier tickets did.\n- **First attempt hung:** my first commit/push attempt hung on a stray command in the script I sent.
